newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Calendar spread crossed in Euro-FTSE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Calendar spread crossed in Euro-FTSE.

text.p: Most of the action in UK equity options on Friday was in the FTSE 100 index where spread trades were established, dealers said.
Spread trades are established when options in a given class are sold in order to reduce the risk of buying the same number of options having a different expiry date, strike price or both.

The largest deal by early afternoon was a crossed trade in European style FTSE in which a calendar spread was established with around 8,500 August 4725 calls traded at 167p, along with the same number of September 4725 calls at 200p, making a net debit/credit of 33p.

The buyer of the spread expects the market to be flat by August expiry so the short calls will expire worthless. The long September calls will then be held if it is believed the market will rally sufficiently such that the long calls will make a profit.
In contrast, the seller of the spread expects the market to be volatile up to August expiry thereby reducing the spread value so that the position can be closed at a profit.
Another large deal in FTSE was a bull spread in which 3,000 June 4825 calls were bought and 3,000 June 4850 calls sold for a net debit of about 8p.
At expiry, this will make a maximum of 16-1/2p if the FTSE index goes above 4,850.
A long straddle was established by one trader expecting increased volatility. It involved buying 1,275 August 4825 puts and calls in FTSE at about 114p and 124p each.
For a profit at expiry, the index needs to be either below 4,587 or above 5,063.
At 1429 GMT, cash FTSE was up 19.8 to 4,777.2 and June FTSE futures were up nine points at 4,780.
